claims.text: Approximately 6 hours of high-energy ball milling induces sufficient lattice strain and grain refinement in equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
The milling-induced lattice strain and grain refinement lower the energy barrier for a metastable FCC/BCC solid-solution transition.
SPS at 1000°C densifies mechanically alloyed CoCrFeNiTi.
SPS at 1000°C does not trigger excessive Ti-driven HCP precipitation in CoCrFeNiTi.
Valence electron concentration and atomic-radius mismatch govern the stability window of the proposed FCC/BCC transition.
The equimolar CoCrFeNiTi composition favors an FCC/BCC solid solution over HCP precipitation at 1000°C.
The initial elemental powder mixture has coarse grains and low lattice strain.
Conventionally cast CoCrFeNiTi has low hardness, high porosity, and a coarse-grained structure.
Controlling the processing atmosphere reduces oxygen contamination and associated TiO formation.
High lattice strain and grain refinement stabilize a metastable FCC/BCC solid solution in CoCrFeNiTi.
Titanium typically drives HCP formation in this alloy at temperatures above the proposed SPS condition.
A Laves phase has been observed in another Ti-containing HEA system.
Annealing conditions and Cr substitution can promote B2/BCC decomposition in Al-Co-Fe-Ni-based HEAs.
The proposed processing route produces a fully dense CoCrFeNiTi bulk alloy with lower porosity than a cast counterpart.
The refined microstructure produces significantly higher Vickers hardness through grain-boundary strengthening.
The processed alloy contains neither brittle HCP phases nor excessive Laves phases.
The threshold for grain growth or phase decomposition in this CoCrFeNiTi alloy lies above 1000°C.
SPS can induce phase changes such as FCC precipitation or solid-solution decomposition involving Laves phases in mechanically alloyed HEAs.
Low-load Vickers hardness testing can isolate grain-boundary strengthening from precipitation hardening.
More than 5% HCP in the 1000°C sample would show that the temperature boundary was exceeded or that VEC and atomic-radius mismatch failed to stabilize the FCC/BCC state.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome calls the alloy fully dense, but the falsification rule permits up to 5% porosity without falsifying that outcome.

The mechanism states that the composition favors the FCC/BCC solid solution over HCP at 1000°C, whereas the uncertainty field acknowledges that this transition and its HCP threshold are not confirmed for CoCrFeNiTi.
The hypothesis describes lowering a thermodynamic energy barrier, while the mechanism describes lowering an activation-energy barrier; these are distinct thermodynamic and kinetic concepts.
